description: The same missionary send as direct-bcc-inline-via-cloudflare, delivered instead through Exchange Online. Pairs with it to isolate what a delivery path mutates.

original.subject: Semana 13 — conferencia de zona y una llanta ponchada

notes: The missionary's signature does not survive this path. Verified with mailauth against the pristine capture: d=missionary.org s=google returns 'body hash did not verify' here, while the byte-identical message delivered through Cloudflare passes. The injected <meta> tag is the whole cause.

Exchange Online omits the authserv-id entirely: the header opens 'Authentication-Results: spf=pass (sender IP is ...)'. RFC 8601 requires that field, so a header with no identifier must match no configured authserv-id rather than being accepted as unlabelled.

Exchange injects <meta http-equiv="Content-Type" content="text/html; charset=utf-8"> at the top of the HTML part. That 84-byte insertion is the only body difference from the Cloudflare copy; all three images are byte-identical across both paths.
Because the HTML is mutated in transit but the plain-text part is not, bodyHead100 must be normalized from text/plain rather than from tag-stripped HTML.
